title: Religion and the Bowman and Rene families
summary: Raised Catholic; describes his German grandfather Bowman, a shipping commissioner, and his father's French-descended family.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: The old Catholic, I was raised a Catholic, and that's the time when the Catholic, I never forget my mother and father at that time, my grandfather was named Bowman, he was shipping commissioner here, what I meant, he had his charge of all the boats that came in from South America, those fruit boats that brought bananas and all the things, all the boats that came in, and they had to go to his office to get okay, and he was well off, there was quite a story behind him before he came to New Orleans, because he was just formerly from Germany, Grandpa Bowman, and he had his home with his children, 11 children, with my grandmother, who was a mother, who was, at that time, she was colored at that time, between colored and part Indian, and she, naturally, they live on Lyon Street, and he was doing very well, one of his, two of his sons were in the post office, and so forth, so they did very well, so Grandpa was the, well, let's see, what was I saying, I was trying to figure out what the plan was, I was talking about, what was I saying? I was talking about your religion. Oh, my religion, yes, and so, so, my dad was kind of, as he saw, but he has kind of a Roman nose like I have, to someone, but he was dark brown skinned, his dad was French, René, his name René, and he was chef, cooked at the St. Charles Hotel, here, chef pastry cook, and so, Papa was allowed to court Mama, although the Mama and the family of the Bowmans were very light-complected, you know, and some of them were, even when, you know, Pastor White, you might say, it was there, you were on the other side, some of them, and, but, she was allowed to come to the house and eventually married Mama. He was, Mama was much older than yours, maybe about five or six years or so, or more, and they, they got married, and, and when he got married, there's this church there on Napoleon, Napoleon and Camp Street called, what was that, St. St. David, I can't, you find the name. We can ride by it, maybe. Yes, the St. David.
